newsitem.title: CHINA: China's A, B indices end up on improved sentiment.
newsitem.headline: China's A, B indices end up on improved sentiment.

text.p: China's A and B share indices closed up on Monday on improved sentiment following last week's gains, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index rose 0.715 points or 1.1 percent to 65.872 points, while Shenzhen's B index jumped 2.83 percent or 4.21 points to end at 153.27 points.
On the A share market, Shanghai's A index gained 5.196 points or 0.52 percent to 1000.698 points and Shenzhen's A index rose 6.13 points or 1.68 percent to finish at 370.81 points.
Brokers said market sentiment had improved a lot after the market's rises last week, which triggered follow-up demand focusing on shares that are expected to post solid 1996 results.
"The market is being supported by optimism over China's overall economy this year and I expect share prices to rise slowly over the medium term," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
"Recent institutional support also helped to improve market sentiment," one Shanghai broker said.
In Shanghai, Huangshan Tourism was the star, jumping $0.432 or 7.54 percent to $0.456 on volume of 593,000 shares.
Chlor Alkali was the most active share on institutional buying, rising $0.014 or 4.66 percent to $0.314 on volume of 1.6 million shares.

In Shenzhen, a strong rise in market heavyweight Changan Automobile coupled with heavy trade boosted investor confidence. Changan soared HK$0.27 to HK$4.80 on the day's most active trade of 4.21 million shares.
Dadonghai Tourism, the sharpest gainer, jumped HK$0.35 or 9.21 percent to HK$4.15 on trade of 3.32 million shares on institutional buying, brokers said.
On the A share markets, Shanghai-listed Lanzhou Minbai was the star on talks of its good results, soaring 1.24 yuan or 10 percent to its limit-up of 13.62 yuan, on volume of 3.9 million shares.
In Shenzhen, Hengyang Chinese Medicine closed at its 10 percent limit-up of 8.43 yuan, with 3.58 million shares traded.
